identificationModule.briefTitle: Improving Women's Fertility Awareness and Reducing Anxiety Through Ovarian Reserve Screening and AI Counseling
identificationModule.officialTitle: Women Rise, Families Thrive: Advancing Women's Health and Fertility Awareness Through Ovarian Reserve Assessment in Hong Kong

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study evaluates the impact of preventive ovarian reserve screening and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled counseling on fertility awareness and reproductive anxiety among women in Hong Kong. Hong Kong faces low birth rates, and reproductive anxiety regarding the biological clock remains a key barrier to family planning. Participants aged 25 to 38 years will be allocated to receive either anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) blood testing combined with counseling or standard health education materials. The study compares an interactive AI conversational agent ("Shelby") with traditional written reports to evaluate whether AI communication improves comprehension of medical results, reduces anxiety, and enhances fertility intentions. Findings aim to inform future public health screening policies.

interventions.name: AI-Enabled Fertility Counseling
interventions.description: An interactive AI conversational agent ('Shelby', shecare.ai) providing personalized, culturally tailored fertility education and AMH test interpretation with built-in safety protocols.

interventions.name: Standard Educational Materials or PDF laboratory reports
interventions.description: Provision of conventional static health education materials via standard medical brochures and/or standard PDF laboratory reports with reference ranges without interactive conversational AI features.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Fertility Intentions and Reproductive Planning

identificationModule.briefTitle: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Breast Cancer Screening: The ANIHTA Study
identificationModule.officialTitle: Introducing Artificial Intelligence in Personalised Breast Screening Programs: a Health Technology Assessment

leadSponsor.name: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate how artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated into an organized breast cancer screening program for women aged 50-74 years undergoing mammography screening.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can an AI-based workflow that identifies selected mammograms for review by a third radiologist improve or maintain the cancer detection rate compared with the current AI-supported double-reading workflow?
* How would this AI-based workflow affect recall rates, biopsy referrals, false-positive results, interval cancers, radiologists' workload, and the number of cases requiring third-reader review?

interventions.name: Artificial intelligence-based software for mammography
interventions.description: Lunit INSIGHT MMG is an artificial intelligence-based software for mammography that generates a continuous malignancy score ranging from 0 to 100. In the retrospective breast screening cohort, AI scores will be used to assess diagnostic performance and to analytically reconstruct alternative AI-supported screening workflow strategies. Strategy A represents the observed routine AI-supported double-reading workflow without third-reader arbitration. Strategy B represents an emulated AI-triggered workflow in which prespecified AI score thresholds (AIpt and AInt) are used to identify selected examinations for offline third-radiologist assessment or direct recall classification. Strategy B will be reconstructed retrospectively and will not be prospectively applied to clinical decision-making or patient management.

interventions.name: Discrete Choice Experiment on AI-Supported Breast Cancer Screening
interventions.description: Healthcare professionals involved in the organized breast cancer screening program will complete a structured Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE) designed to assess preferences regarding the organizational and clinical integration of artificial intelligence into breast cancer screening. The DCE will evaluate acceptability, usability, trust in AI, perceived utility, satisfaction, and preferences regarding alternative characteristics of AI-supported screening workflows. The survey is observational and does not modify clinical practice or patient management.
